{{distinguish|Schottky form}}
In [[algebraic geometry]], the Schottky–Klein '''prime form''' ''E''(''x'',''y'') of a [[compact space|compact]] [[Riemann surface]] ''X'' depends on two elements ''x'' and ''y'' of ''X'', and vanishes if and only if ''x''&nbsp;=&nbsp;''y''.  The prime form ''E'' is not quite a holomorphic function on ''X''&nbsp;×&nbsp;''X'', but is a section of a holomorphic line bundle over this space. Prime forms were introduced by [[Friedrich Schottky]] and [[Felix Klein]].

Prime forms can be used to construct meromorphic functions on ''X'' with given poles and zeros. If Σ''n''<sub>''i''</sub>''a''<sub>''i''</sub> is a divisor linearly equivalent to 0, then Π''E''(''x'',''a''<sub>''i''</sub>)<sup>''n''<sub>''i''</sub></sup> is a meromorphic function with given poles and zeros.
